title: Body vertical gradient: derive top/bottom from spine-normal (no world-up fallback)
description:
## Summary
The Body vertical-gradient appearance computes its top/bottom (dorsal/ventral) blend from a hard-coded WORLD +Y axis in `BodyVerticalGradientSampler.TryGetBodySample` (`verticalRaw = (position.y - centerline.y) / radius`). For the `dinus_uprightus` creature the gradient does not follow the spine's perpendicular normal axis; it is simply the Y axis. Fix: derive the top/bottom axis from the body frame spine-normal (seeded from `Forward`, the same axis the editor scale/gizmo and skeleton use), and expose that derived feature for future consumers.

## User Mandate
> "It needs to allow for defining a 'back' (the top) and a 'belly' (the bottom)."

> "Option B, it should be fully derived. I always intended the spine-normal method, so this is the ONLY implementation, no legacy world up fallback. Back and belly are not the specific terms. Top/bottom are correct, but given a gradient and the proper axis alignment, that is the type of creature this could create that has a lighter belly and darker back like real creatures. The back is seeded from forward, or possibly whatever this scale gizmo uses. The SpineNormal is a derived feature, but is a useful one that should probably be exposed on the creature for other future consumers"

STRICT. Binding constraints (must not be relaxed/re-scoped without user confirmation):
- Spine-normal is the ONLY implementation; there is NO legacy world-up fallback in the vertical gradient.
- The gradient axis is FULLY DERIVED (Option B) — no authored back/belly vector in DNA.
- Top/bottom are the correct terms (not back/belly): top gradient = the dorsal/darker side, bottom = the ventral/lighter-belly side, like real creatures.
- The reference used to seed the derived axis is the creature `Forward` — equivalently the same body-frame +Y axis the editor scale/gizmo and skeleton already use (`BodyFrame.Normal`).
- The derived SpineNormal should be exposed on the creature for other future consumers.

## Scope
- `Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Appearance/BodyVerticalGradientSampler.cs`: replace world-Y vertical sample with the spine-normal projection.
- `Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Definition/CreaturePartWorldTransformResolver.cs` (`ResolvedCreatureSnapshot`): expose precomputed per-sample BodyFrames (spine normal) as a derived feature.
- Thread precomputed frames into the bake call sites (`AppearanceBaker`, `PartAppearanceSampler`) so the per-vertex gradient does not re-transport frames.
- Update/add tests in `Assets/Scripts/Tests/Runtime/BodyVerticalGradientAppearanceTests.cs`.
- No DNA schema / serialization / canonicalizer / validator change (Option B = no new authored field).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `verticalSample` (+1 top gradient, -1 bottom) is computed from the body-frame spine-normal at the point, not world Y.
- No authored DNA field added.
- Per-sample body frames (spine normals) are exposed on `ResolvedCreatureSnapshot`.
- The gradient bake reuses precomputed frames (no per-vertex O(n) frame transport).
- Horizontal-body gradient tests still pass; the sloped-body test is updated to spine-normal semantics; a curved/upright-spine test proves top/bottom follows the frame normal where it differs from world Y.
- Deterministic; Runtime code stays scene/editor-API free.

## Validation
Compile runtime + test assemblies; run the focused `BodyVerticalGradientAppearanceTests`; then the broader Runtime suite in Unity when available. Record results here.

## Findings
(implementation evidence added as comments)

## Blockers
Unity availability for the full Runtime/PlayMode suite is to be confirmed at validation time.

## Next Step
Implement across sampler, snapshot exposure, bake call sites, and tests.

comments.body:
Implementation complete (Option B, spine-normal only, no world-up fallback).

Files changed (uncommitted):
- `Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Appearance/BodyVerticalGradientSampler.cs`: vertical sample is now `Dot(position - centerline, spineNormal)/radius` where spineNormal is the body-frame Normal (Forward-seeded, parallel-transported), spherically interpolated per segment. Added a frames-aware `TryGetBodySample`/`EvaluateColor` for the bake so frames are transported once, not per vertex. No authored axis; no world-up gradient branch.
- `Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Definition/CreaturePartWorldTransformResolver.cs` (`ResolvedCreatureSnapshot`): exposes derived `BodyFrame[] BodyFrames` (one per sample) as the shared spine-normal feature for future consumers; computed once in `Resolve`.
- `Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Appearance/AppearanceBaker.cs` + `PartAppearanceSampler.cs`: bake reuses `snapshot.BodyFrames` (or derives once) per bake.
- `Assets/Scripts/Tests/Runtime/BodyVerticalGradientAppearanceTests.cs`: replaced the world-up sloped-body test with `EvaluateColor_UprightSpine_TopFollowsForwardSeededNormal_NotWorldY` (discriminates vs world Y on an upright spine) and added `Snapshot_ExposesBodyFrames_SpineNormalsUnitAndPerpendicularToTangents`.

No DNA schema / serialization / canonicalizer / validator change (Option B).

Validation evidence:
- `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Runtime.csproj --no-restore` -> 0 warnings/0 errors.
- `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime.csproj --no-restore` -> 0 warnings/0 errors.
- PlayMode `ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime` in Unity: 520/520 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (4.25s), job 6187bb6200b64a4e95d28923c861ff9a.
- `git diff --check` clean.

Residual risk: behavior change for any creature whose body is not level (top/bottom now follows the creature's own dorsal line rather than world height) — this is the intended mandate. Not committed (commit not requested).
